thread:
Maria L: Quick proposal — add a "stealth degrade" option to automatic fallback policies. It would return minimal structured responses (200 OK + small JSON) instead of full model output when error triggers fire.

Kevin P: Can you sketch the UX? how would teams configure/see this in Console?

Maria L: Two quick pieces — policy page gets a toggle for "Stealth (minimal response)" and a severity slider (info/warn/critical). The rollout flow shows a live sample of what the minimal response looks like.

Raj S: I like the idea. One risk: integrations that expect generated text might break. We should add a compatibility shim (header + opt-in) — e.g., X-Redwood-Degrade: stealth.

Olivia C: UX nit: show a small simulator on the policy editor where you can paste a failing request and preview the degraded payload. Also add a one-click "preview in prod" but gated by feature flag.

Kevin P: How do we detect the trigger? Current triggers are error-rate, latency-percentile, and explicit error codes. Do we add "semantic failure" signals from eval hooks?

Maria L: Proposed triggers: 1) infra errors (5xx), 2) model-completion-timeouts, 3) quality-signal from evals (drift above threshold). For 3 we need a small API: /v1/policies/:id/notify-eval -> boolean.

Raj S: API debate: name it policy.signal or policy.notify? We should keep consistency with existing rollout APIs. Current is /v1/rollouts/{id}/events. I'd prefer /v1/policies/{id}/events to keep resource first.

Kevin P: My vote: /v1/policies/{id}/signals. Short, meaningful.

Maria L: OK tally: signals it is. Also need audit fields. Every automatic fallback decision must emit an audit event with: trigger_type, matched_rule, time, request_id, decision (stealth|variant|fallback-model).

Olivia C: For Console, show audit replay: timeline that groups by request_id and allows playback of original request -> degraded response. That helps customers validate.

Raj S: Implementation detail: we'll capture minimal KU (key user) data to support replay but stay GDPR-friendly — strip PII by default and provide customer opt-in to include full inputs.

Kevin P: Can we use existing tracing? e.g., attach trace_id to the audit event. Then Console can fetch traces for context.

Maria L: Yes, attach trace_id and span_id. Also add a retention policy per org: 7/30/90/365 days.

deploy-bot: Deployment started for feature/stealth-degrade-api at commit d3f9a2. CI: ✅, Integration tests: ✅

Olivia C: Edge case: when stealth degrade is active for a route that also uses function/tool-calls. What do we return? Minimal structured response should include a tools list with a flag "skipped_due_to_degrade".

Raj S: Good call. Also we should ensure downstream SDKs treat stealth as non-error (status 200) but surface a new field: "degraded": true. Docs must be explicit.

Kevin P: Telemetry question: we need separate counters — stealth_active, stealth_invoked, stealth_duration, and latency buckets for degraded responses. Add them to exporter spec.

Maria L: I'll draft the telemetry schema. Also want an admin action in Console: "Force-simulate-degrade for N requests" so SEs can test without causing a real incident.

Olivia C: UX flow for rollouts: when you ramp policy, show a projected % of traffic that will be affected (based on historical signals). If projected impact > X% show a warning.

Raj S: Security check: audit events must be signed and available in customer audit log with integrity metadata.

sre-oncall: From ops POV — add an escape-hatch endpoint: /v1/admin/policies/{id}/pause that can be called by paging tools. It should immediately stop automatic fallbacks for a policy.

Maria L: Good. We'll put pause behind RBAC and require a justification string in the call. Also surface last_paused_by + reason in Console.

Kevin P: One more API design decision: when policy applies stealth degrade, do we mutate the response on the gateway layer or inside the runtime? Mutating at gateway is easier for consistency across deployments (hosted/dedicated/private).

Raj S: Gateway mutation is simpler for audit capture. But runtime has better access to model internal signals. Maybe hybrid: runtime emits a proposed decision, gateway enforces and records final audit event.

Maria L: That hybrid sounds right. Runtime evaluates triggers, emits decision proto, gateway verifies policy and writes final audit + response.

Olivia C: I'll mock the Console panels and simulator today and share screenshots in #design later.

Maria L: I'll create a short RFC with schema examples and endpoints: /v1/policies/{id}/signals, /v1/policies/{id}/audit, /v1/admin/policies/{id}/pause. Will attach telemetry spec and RBAC notes.

Kevin P: Thanks — keen to see the RFC. If we can get a small dogfood early that'd be great. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Deployment finished for feature/stealth-degrade-api. Canary: 10% traffic. Monitoring: enabled.

Maria L: Canary note — let's watch stealth_invoked over the next 6 hours and check Console replay for false positives.

Olivia C: copied. I'll set up a short dashboard with the key metrics and a playback widget.

Raj S: tagging @kevin for API naming confirmation and @sre-oncall for pause endpoint acceptance tests.

Kevin P: Ack, will review the RFC today.
